item: A URL's userinfo is out of a link's domain label, the feed key, the canonical URL and the feed preflight's host, read after the last @ as the fetcher does (R628)
refs: R628 R634 R637 R621 R624 PR pending
summary: R628 (Plan 01:53Z: fold the userinfo labels into R621's masking, a follow-up after R624, with two security reads and a test that the canonical key dedupes the credentialed and plain forms of one URL; the four places are R624's row's 'same pattern elsewhere' list). Each now reads a URL's host as the fetcher does: what follows the LAST @ of the authority, as urllib.parse reads it. BEFORE: (1) src/services/link_analyzer/extractor.py kept the userinfo in a link's domain label (main path, regex fallback, and the label the social/ad/tracking substring checks search), so https://twitter.com:x@news.example/a read as social, and internal against external compared two whole netlocs, so a link to the page's own host written with a userinfo, a port or www. read as external and was stored as an outbound ArticleLink, credentials included; (2) src/database/feed_key.py kept the userinfo in the feed identity, so one feed written with and without credentials was two sources; (3) src/utils/url_utils.py kept it in canonicalize_url, get_domain_from_url and get_base_url, so the dedup read one page as two (a crawl from a credentialed start fetched the page again without them) and the credentials reached the stored canonical_url; (4) src/monitoring/feed_preflight.py put it in a report's host field, and the robots read built from that host sent it (requests turns it into Authorization: Basic). NOW: (1) _host_label (the host and port, lower-cased) is the domain label at all three sites; _site (the host after the last @, without its port or www.; written in the module so it does not load src.ingest, R621, and held equal to src.ingest.crawl._registrable_host by a test) decides internal: same-host spellings are internal and are no longer stored as outbound links; another host stays external; two empty hosts are no site. (2) feed_key drops the userinfo; read_feed_key reads a stored key holding an @ as its row's feed key today (exact: a key written since R628 holds an @ only where it is not a userinfo, and re-deriving gives it back). (3) canonicalize_url drops the userinfo (url-v2); CANON_VERSION moves url-v1 -> url-v2 by its own rule (bump whenever canonicalize_url changes its rules); the boot self-heal that backfills canon_version on rows predating the column now writes url-v1, as the Alembic revision d3e4f5a6b7c8 does (CANON_VERSION alone would have stamped url-v1 rows url-v2). (4) the preflight's host is the fetcher's host key (_host_netloc with the URL's scheme: lower-cased, its default port gone), so the report and the robots read carry no userinfo; the sampled feed itself is still fetched as given. The page request everywhere still carries the URL as written (R621). CONTINUITY, per stored identity: articles.canonical_url (indexed, not unique; written by pipeline/batch from canonicalize_url; read by the pre-fetch dedup in ingest_url and the crawl, the in-memory dedup front, link_preview's lookup; evidence bundles, custody records and the runlog export carry the stored value, never recompute it): rows stored before R628 keep their canonical_url, credentials included, and their url-v1 stamp; nothing rewrites them. Without a fallback, an article stored from a credentialed URL would be fetched again on every pass that lists it (the content hash then names it a duplicate, after the request; a changed page would be stored a second time). Fallback added: pipeline._canonical_stored, used by ingest_url (the crawl's dedup reads the canonical form alone since the R628 reads: R630 drops a harvested link with a userinfo before it, and the start URL never passes it), asks url_v1_canonical's form on a miss, only for a URL whose authority holds an @ (one indexed query; the dedup front is not marked with it, so it stays exact). Stated: link_preview for the plain URL does not find an article whose stored canonical_url holds credentials (it still matches Article.url as given). sources.feed_key (UNIQUE (domain, feed_key); derived on every ORM write by the before_insert/before_update event, re-derived by the source-topics bulk UPDATE and the curated-stamp heal; read by source_lookup's add and YAML-import lookups, the CSV import, the seeder's pairing and the restore merge's SQL join): a key stored before R628 stays until its row's next ORM write (an edit, enable/disable, a qualification verdict, the crawl's last_crawled_at stamp), which re-derives it without the userinfo (unless another row of the domain holds that feed, R634 below). Fallback added: read_feed_key in source_for_feed (only on a miss, only the domain's keys holding an @), source_for_import and csv_io.upsert_sources, so adding or importing the same feed again edits the legacy row instead of making a second one. Not added in R628 (R634 below closes the first for the URL's own login, the R628 reads' rule 2b for another login and for the plain URL): the restore merge compared the stored column in SQL (a domain with one source on each side still matched by its one-to-one fallback; with several, an incoming copy of a local legacy-keyed feed landed as a new sibling until the local row healed). Stated: the seeder compares stored keys (the bundled catalogue holds no credentialed URL, so a legacy key never matched a catalogue entry and still does not; once healed, a credentialed operator row pairs with the catalogue entry of the same feed and the three-way merge keeps the operator's URL). R634 (the coordinator's ruling, 02:56Z, option b, on the duplicate-pair cost this row had left needing a ruling): when a re-derived feed_key would meet another row's key, that row keeps its stored key, so no write, bulk update or restore fails, and the pair stays two rows. BEFORE (759d39cfa): a domain holding one feed twice, as a build before R628 could store it (https://news.example/rss and https://alice:hunter2@news.example/rss, or two logins), derived one key for both, so the credentialed row's next ORM write failed UNIQUE (domain, feed_key) (the crawl lane's stamp was rolled back and the outlet stayed due), the daily source-topics bulk UPDATE failed whole, the curated stamp's heal at boot failed the same way (a fourth path, found here), restoring a backup holding the pair into an empty store or a store holding its credentialed row failed at the source INSERT, into a store holding the plain row (or both) filed both halves under the plain row, and an add or an import of the credentialed URL found the plain row and wrote over it. NOW: src/database/feed_key.py: legacy_feed_key (the key a build before R628 derived: the userinfo kept), keeps_a_stored_key (the gate, no I/O: the stored key holds an @, is its own URL's pre-R628 key and differs from today's; a row whose URL was edited since does not pass, so an edit onto a twin's feed is still refused by UNIQUE), key_to_write (today's key, or the stored key when another row of the domain stores today's key or would take it on its next write: its own URL's key, so a stale-keyed twin counts; two credentialed rows of one feed both keep theirs, so the order of writes never decides), domain_keys and lookup_key (the import and add readings). src/database/models.py: source_key_to_write is the ONE reading for every writer that re-derives a stored row's key, the before_update event (the crawl lane's stamp and every ORM write; a kept key leaves the column out of the UPDATE), the source-topics bulk UPDATE (src/analytics/source_topics.py: a kept row goes in a second executemany without the column) and the curated stamp's heal (src/catalog/qualification.py: a kept row is left out of the fixes). COST: a string check per written row; the collision query only for a row that passes the gate, ONE query on idx_source_domain (the domain's other rows, compared in Python; its parameters are the domain and the id, never a key or a URL). An INSERT through the ORM always derives today's key, and source_key_to_write reads the database, not the flush: a pair is landed by a restore, and one flush that heals a row and also inserts its feed, or edits another row onto it, raises UNIQUE and is rolled back (no current writer does: an add finds the row first, an edit onto a held feed is refused first, the CSV import writes one record per savepoint). RESTORE (src/backup/merge.py): _incoming_feed_keys, registered as oo_inc_feed_key in place of oo_feed_key in _same_source, the legacy-store refusal and the INSERT, keys an incoming source whose URL carries a userinfo under the store's pre-R628 key of that URL when the store holds it, else the key of the store's row with exactly that URL, else its own pre-R628 key when another incoming source of the domain derives the same key today, else today's key (one query on the domain's index per such URL, its rows compared in Python). WHAT EACH PATH DOES WITH THE PAIR: an ORM write, the bulk UPDATE and the heal write both rows and keep both keys; a restore of the pair into an empty store, a store holding the plain row, the credentialed row or both lands two rows, each half's articles under its own row; into a store whose one row of the feed already healed (it holds the feed once), both halves are that row (local wins, stated); the credentialed half restored alone beside the pair is its own row, and beside the plain row alone it is that row (R628 unchanged). An add or an import of either URL finds its own row (source_lookup.source_for_feed reads the domain's keys holding an @ first; source_for_import and the CSV import match each stored row under domain_keys and each record under lookup_key), which also closes the restore gap stated above for a credentialed URL. Stated: an import file holding both halves into a store holding one row reads them as one feed (R628); a kept key holds its login until one row of the pair is deleted, and then heals on that row's next write; source_identity.backfill_feed_keys and the composite rebuild run only on a store still keyed on the domain alone, which cannot hold a pair. REDACTION (of the key; the URL itself is R637's, below): no module that answers, reports, exports or shows names the column (checked: src/api, src/static, src/monitoring, the doctor, the diagnostics bundle, the CSV and YAML exports; a test lists the fourteen modules that do and fails on a fifteenth); a kept key is never a parameter of a write and the merge reads the store's rows by domain only (tests record every statement's parameters and the merge's reads); the restore report's sibling feed is written through failure_url (***@), as R621's readers write a URL, where it showed the feed URL as given; a database driver's error text stays withheld by record_text wherever it is recorded. R637 (the coordinator's ruling, 04:15Z, on Steward 3's R628+R634 read, finding 1: rss_url itself carried the login, unmasked, in the source answers, the exports and the backups, so keeping it out of the key changed nothing a person could see). SHOWN MASKED, through fetch_verdict.shown_url (failure_url's form: the userinfo as ***@; None and "" as they are): src/api/source_management.py's source list, one source, a group's sources, the search, the discovered-sources answer and both discovery answers (url, rss_url and rss_urls); src/api/main.py's legacy /api/sources, with or without fields; src/api/source_io.py's catalogue list (the Sources tab); src/monitoring/health.py's probed URL. The create and update request logs write the body with its rss_url masked, and the duckduckgo demo prints mask theirs; no other log line in src/ writes an rss_url (the fetcher's own sentences already go through failure_url, R620/R621). The stored value is unchanged, and the fetch, the discovery and the health probe use it, login included. KEPT AS WRITTEN, stated, so they round-trip: the CSV export (source_io._source_to_row), the YAML file export (SourceManager.export_sources_to_yaml), GET /api/sources/export (the YAML export's JSON form; JSON is YAML, import_sources_from_yaml reads it back, and the UI does not show it) and the backups (the merge copies rss_url). The Sources tab says so beside "Export all (CSV)" and the backup panel says so for a backup, each a visible card-caveat line with the long form on hover, in all 12 locales. R637, amended 2026-11-09 06:13Z (the coordinator, with Steward 3's GO): a backup made without encryption is a plain file, like the export, so the backup line also says "A backup made without encryption is a plain file, so keep it private." and the hover both lines share ends "The export, like a backup made without encryption, is a plain file, so keep it private."; the export's own line is unchanged, and a backup keeps the URL as written, encrypted or not (3 strings, the two changed ones replaced in place in every locale; i18n_report --min 100: 7,415 keys, every locale complete; the chrome audit 0 unkeyed; the glossary 0 violations). THE EDIT PATH, fetch_verdict.url_to_store, used by PUT /api/sources/{id}, POST /api/sources/ and POST /api/sources/discover/add (the three routes that take an rss_url from the UI; the batch routes take none, and the CSV and YAML imports read a file as written): the masked form of the row's stored URL is that stored URL, so a form saved unchanged keeps the login; a URL with no userinfo, or another one typed, is stored as sent; the mask on the same scheme, host and port (the fetcher's host key) takes the stored login, so a path edit keeps it; the mask anywhere else (another host, port or scheme, https to http included) is dropped, so a login never goes there and *** is never stored as a user name. Stated: a login that is literally *** cannot be set through a form; feed_preflight's url field holds bundled-catalogue URLs (not an rss_url, no login) and is unchanged; a web URL a discovery found is masked in the answer too, and posting it back stores it without the mask. THE R628 READS (Steward 3's and the independent read of R628+R634, folded on the coordinator's defaults): a page's <link> is typed exactly as an anchor (its branch asked the parsed URL for a rel it never has, so every <link> was external, and a page's own <link href="/rss"> was stored as an ArticleLink with the page's login). Removing that branch is a behaviour change, stated: every <link> used to be external, and now one is read as an anchor: internal when it names the page's own site (no longer stored) and external otherwise. PUT /api/sources/{id} answers an edit onto a feed another row of the domain holds with 409 in the add's words (source_lookup.FEED_HELD, "Source with domain ... and this feed already exists"): the plain row of a pair edited to its twin's exact URL is refused before the write (url_held_by_another: the twin keeps its own key, so the unique index cannot see it); a new login on the kept row of a plain+login pair derives the plain row's key, the unique index refuses it as before, and after the rollback it is answered as that refusal only when another row of the domain stores the key the write would store (feed_held_by_another, read back from the store, never from the driver's text; any other IntegrityError stays the handler's class-only 500, and is raised on with its parameters hidden, exc.hide_parameters set before the bare raise (Steward 3's low with the GO: its text carried the UPDATE's parameters, the stored address and its login among them, to uvicorn's "Exception in ASGI application" line, the one the url-v1 read's error reached; it is the one re-raise of a database error in the routes R637 and the reads touched, the rest are raw sqlite3 in the merge, whose errors carry no parameters, or catch and do not raise)); an edit that leaves the domain and the feed as they are is not asked. match_import takes source_for_feed's read_feed_key fallback (import_reads), so on a two-logins pair the plain URL or a third login is the oldest row by the add, source_for_import and the CSV import alike. Restore rule 2b: an incoming source rules 1 and 2 did not place is the store's row whose pre-R628 key reads as its feed's key today, when no rule took that row and no row of the domain stores today's key (another login beside an unhealed alice@ row, or the plain URL beside a lone legacy row, is that row, where it landed as a sibling and, since R634, stayed one); URLs with a userinfo first, so a backup's pair files its credentialed half there and lands its plain half as its own row; the oldest such row; cost: one query with no parameter for the store's keys holding an "@", and one on (domain, feed_key) per candidate, today's key holding no login. The crawl's url-v1 dedup read is removed (dead code: R630 drops a harvested link with a userinfo before it). The pipeline's extract-failed and non-article log lines write the URL through failure_url. The url-v1 dedup read's database error hides its parameter (SQLAlchemy's hide_parameters, set on the error before it is raised again): the app's catches read it through record_text, but POST /api/ingest's error reaches the server's own "Exception in ASGI application" line, written as the exception made its message behind a filter that takes out passphrases only. The test ratchet also fails on a module that reads every column of sources without naming the key (SELECT * or s.* from it, Source.__table__ or __mapper__, inspect(Source), a getattr over a column's name, its column listing by name; allowed with its reason: database/maintenance.py's boot migrations, which read which columns exist); it cannot see a table name built at run time, an ORM row handed whole to a serializer (no route does), an attribute name held in data, or a copy of the file itself; the parameter recorder listens on the Engine class, so a path that opens its own engine is heard. The preflight host: data/feed_preflight.jsonl is a log; its records' host values are written at run time, and the bundled market, index and calendar catalogues hold no credentialed URL, so no stored record has one. The extractor's domain label is not stored; ArticleLink rows already stored from same-host links stay (links are extracted only at ingest). ENGINE STAMP: tests/test_index_engine_stamp.py: the canonical URL and the feed key are not index inputs (index_inputs_digest reads text, title, languages, date, country and self-name forms); feed_key.py is NOT_OUTPUT_AFFECTING (a pass loads it, never writes sources) and gains no import, so the closure, the pins and INDEXER_VERSION are unchanged. IMPORT COST: no new import in the extractor, url_utils, feed_key or source_lookup (pure string helpers); feed_preflight already imported src.ingest at top level; a fresh-interpreter test pins that the four still import without src.ingest. TESTS: tests/test_userinfo_labels_r628.py, 107 cases, through the real crawl_source and ingest_url over an in-memory session, _maybe_index_links, create_source, upsert_sources, the YAML import, merge_corpus and run_feed_preflight. On 6dd9b14fe (the R624 fold) 36 bug cases fail, the 35 cases of the three new helpers (_site, read_feed_key, url_v1_canonical) fail because they do not exist there, and the 30 controls and 6 continuity cases pass; on this branch all 107 pass. 437 related existing test files, test_index_engine_stamp.py and test_article_identity_seams.py among them: 9,141 passed; the two failures (test_shared_file_writes on src/ingest/__init__.py's three unconverted write sites, and test_source_coverage_rollup's mean-tone case, this venv lacking vaderSentiment) fail the same way on 6dd9b14fe, in files this change does not touch; test_awareness.py and test_commodity.py were left out, as this venv cannot import them (vaderSentiment, scipy). On 759d39cfa (local/r628 after the R630 fix) 28 bug cases fail (the ORM writes, the bulk update, the curated heal, the restores into an empty store and into a store holding the credentialed row, and the two stale twins on UNIQUE (domain, feed_key); the crawl lane with 0 sources crawled; the other restores, the add and the two imports on the wrong row), the 18 cases of the new helpers fail because they do not exist there, and the 9 controls, the stated healed-store restore and the two pins pass; on this branch all 58 pass. R637 TESTS: tests/test_rss_url_masked_r637.py, 33 cases, through the TestClient over a file store (every source answer, the group, both discovery answers and the discovered-sources add on stand-ins, the PUT and the POST, the request logs), check_source on a stand-in probe, export_csv with upsert_sources, the YAML exports with their import, and merge_corpus; every answer is checked for the password anywhere in its body. Three first read as survivors because the runner counted a captured log line that starts with ERROR as a test error; the corrected runner kills them on a named FAILED test. NOT CHANGED, stated: the extractor's normalize_url still keeps a cross-host link's userinfo in ArticleLink.normalized_url (only a link to another site that carries its own login: a link to the page's own site, a <link> element included since the R628 reads, is internal and never stored), a stored identity read by co-citation, link_preview and the articles-by-link lookup (not one of the four places; it needs its own continuity read); the url column of each preflight record still holds the feed URL as given; feed_key's fallback for a URL urllib.parse cannot read keeps its lower-cased text, userinfo included; Article.url and ArticleLink.url keep the URL as given (data handed back, R621); the pre-fetch dedup binds the url-v1 canonical of a URL with a userinfo, login included, as the parameter of one indexed query (it finds an article stored before R628), and a database error on it hides that parameter (the server's own log wrote it whole until the R628 reads) while the app's callers read it through record_text, class only (tested); stays outside, stated: any other statement that binds a URL as given (an article's INSERT binds Article.url, R621) is quoted by an error that escapes POST /api/ingest to that server line, and so, stated, is an IntegrityError on POST /api/sources/ or /api/sources/discover/add (their INSERT binds rss_url as written; neither route catches one, and the add returns the row already holding the feed first, so only a concurrent writer reaches it); a full backup carries a kept key beside rss_url, the same login R637 keeps in rss_url there; canonicalize_url returns a URL urllib.parse cannot read unchanged (only a page's own canonical link can reach it). Pre-existing, unchanged: feed_key keeps a default port (news.example:443/rss is not news.example/rss) where the fetcher's _host_netloc drops it. Release-notes line: «A user name and password written into a web address no longer become part of how the app recognises a page, a feed or a site: the same page or feed written with and without them is now one, they no longer reach a stored article's canonical address or the feed check's report, and a link to an article's own site written with a login, a port or "www." is no longer counted as a link to another site. A feed already stored twice, with and without a login, stays as two entries. A user name and password written into a feed's address are no longer shown anywhere the app shows that address; the source export and the backups keep them as written so a re-imported or restored feed can still be fetched, and the export, like a backup made without encryption, is a plain file, so keep it private. Changing a source to a feed its site already has is refused with a message instead of an internal error. (R628, R634, R637)»
